t: Faulty Keyboard — Direction Flag with Deque
o: Typing 'i' reverses everything typed so far; other characters append normally. Rather than physically reversing (O(n) per 'i'), note that reversal only flips whether new characters attach to the right or the left end. Maintain a deque and a boolean 'rev': normal characters go to the back when not reversed and to the front when reversed; 'i' toggles 'rev'. At the end, reverse the collected sequence iff 'rev' is true. For "string", the single 'i' toggles once, so the tail "rtsng" built backwards becomes "rtsng" reversed appropriately — output "rtsng". For "poiinter", two 'i's cancel out, leaving plain appending with the 'i's removed: "ponter".
k: Reversal is equivalent to switching the insertion end — a deque with a direction flag replaces O(n) reversals.
Each 'i' toggles the flag; the final string is reversed iff the flag is set at the end.
'i' itself is never written to the screen.

a.i: Append characters to the back when rev is false and to the front when rev is true. Because a reversal mirrors the entire buffer, characters typed during 'reversed mode' must come out first, which front-insertion achieves. One final conditional reversal finishes the job.
s: Create an empty deque and rev = false.
For each character: if 'i', toggle rev; else append to back (rev false) or front (rev true).
Join the deque; reverse the joined string if rev is true.
a.t: O(n) — each character handled once; deque operations are O(1).
a.sp: O(n) — the deque holds the output.

a.i: Keep the text as a list and literally reverse it on every 'i'. With n <= 100 this O(n^2) approach is instantaneous and the easiest to verify against the examples by hand.
s: On 'i', reverse the list; otherwise append the character.
a.t: O(n^2) worst case — each 'i' triggers an O(n) reversal; fine for n <= 100.

w: Use the deque version to show algorithmic maturity; the simulation is a fine fallback. Edge cases: strings of all 'i's (empty output), consecutive 'i's canceling, and the guarantee s[0] != 'i' (so the screen is never empty mid-reversal concerns). Follow-up: what if typing 'i' reverses only the last k characters, or deletes them?
